tours.title: A Mamlūk chronicle: Ibn Taġrībirdī's *al-Nujūm al-zāhira*

stops.title: Overview
stops.text: The whole book scores highest as a chronicle. Read window by window, a smaller biographical component appears.

stops.title: Through the text
stops.text:
Each point is a window of about 3,000 words, stepped along the text.
Most windows read as chronicle, but biographical passages take the lead again and again, above all in the second half of the book.

stops.title: Through the text, with headers
stops.text:
The black lines are the book's level-1 headers: they mostly mark the terms of the governors and the reigns of the sultans of Egypt.
Dashed lines would mean headers from a not yet fully annotated version.

stops.title: Entropy compared
stops.text: Entropy measures how varied the vocabulary is. This book sits above most chronicles.

stops.title: Similar books
stops.text: The works whose vocabulary is closest — mostly other chronicles.

stops.title: Author
stops.text: Ibn Taġrībirdī also wrote a biographical dictionary, *al-Manhal al-ṣāfī*. Compare its profile: same author, different type.
